analysis: probe validity: do probe-loss deltas between candidates predict final-loss deltas across seeds?
design: re-run of gate3-probe-loss-384 (seeds 3000-3383, steps=48, cap=4, 2 probe batches) with probe landscape recording; counterfactual branches force candidate k in {1,2,3} at the FIRST mutation event only (branch 0 = default greedy run); per-seed Spearman between the 4 candidates' probe losses and their realized final losses; H1: mean rho > 0 (one-tailed t across seeds, alpha=0.05), pre-registered
interpretation: probe loss is a statistically significant but weak predictor of realized outcome (rho ~ 0.11). Its main value is avoiding the worst candidates rather than identifying the single best one (concordance near chance; avoided excess 0.086 vs left-on-table 0.060). A weak per-event signal accumulated over only 3 mutation events is consistent with the marginal Gate 3 pass and motivates the cadence study.
